steps.instruction: Extract the complete official setup ZIP for your system into a separate writable folder you control. This is a setup package: its launcher prepares the game from your own matching disc through upstream generation/build. On Linux, follow the selected version’s prerequisites, including CMake, Ninja, Python 3 and a C/C++ compiler where required; bundled Windows tools do not supply Linux tools. Downloading and extracting do not run a launcher, compiler or game. Native setup and gameplay remain unqualified by this handoff.

steps.title: Supply the matching original files
steps.instruction: Follow the upstream guide for the version you downloaded. Use your own original in its supported image representation, keeping a CUE and every referenced track together when required, and supply your own BIOS whenever that guide requires it. Preserve the exact edition, disc layout and BIOS requirements in that guide; an included setup BIOS does not establish game compatibility.

steps.title: Finish upstream setup, then add the player
steps.instruction: Deliberately open the supported upstream launcher when you are ready to generate/build from your own files. Follow that version’s completed-player instructions and keep its runtime/compiler companions together. In Portcove choose the resulting native game executable or supported upstream launcher with its supplied working folder. If setup created it elsewhere, select that location. Saving launch details and Play are separate Portcove actions. You or upstream manage runtime updates, original files, saves and settings; these external files are outside Portcove-managed backups. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

steps.title: Use permitted existing copies and local preparation
steps.instruction: Keep permitted copies of reNut and NutStaller, and point NutStaller at your player folder. If extract-xiso is missing, its separate Get extract-xiso action downloads that tool. Then use 3. Pick ISO + extract with your own USA Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts Xbox 360 ISO and 4. Add title update with your matching original update as required by the current release instructions. Back up the prepared folder before approving its replacement. These local preparation actions do not acquire another runtime; Get latest reNut and Do everything do and require separate acquisition permission. Portcove does not run the tools during discovery.

steps.title: Keep the richer upstream launcher available
steps.instruction: NutStaller provides runtime update checks, controls, Workshop and save tools; keep it available after registering the prepared player. steps.title: Add the prepared player, then choose Play
steps.instruction: On Windows select the prepared renut.exe; on Linux select the prepared renut.AppImage and its matching folder. Save the launch details, then choose Play separately. No game, installer or helper is executed merely by discovering or registering the copy.

steps.title: Preserve actual saves, settings and custom content
steps.instruction: Close the game before backup or replacement. Keep your actual selected user-data root; defaults are Documents/renut on Windows and XDG_DATA_HOME/renut, normally ~/.local/share/renut, on Linux. Keep renut.cfg and renut.toml beside the Windows player or in Linux user data, plus the original ISO/update, prepared game and DLC, mods, Workshop content and nutstaller.ini beside the helper. Beta12 also documents custom music in music/ beside the Windows player or ~/.local/share/renut/music on Linux; preserve that folder separately from any custom save path.

steps.title: Keep update and removal ownership clear
steps.instruction: You or upstream update this runtime. Preserve the working copy and actual data before accepting an upstream replacement; a save-tool backup does not establish that every separate mod, music, source or helper folder was included. Portcove registration offers no managed Update, Backup or Rollback and does not adopt these files. Removing the registration preserves every external file.

listings.name: Blood (Raze)
listings.summary: Play Blood in Raze using your own original PC game files.

steps.title: Use your recognized original game files
steps.instruction: Use your own original PC Blood data folder, including BLOOD.RFF, SOUNDS.RFF, BLOOD.INI and its accompanying art/data. Raze recognizes specific Blood 1.0, 1.1 and One Unit Whole Blood identities. Keep optional Cryptic Passage files with their required base data. A remaster player executable is not the original data archive. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze, or add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

steps.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
steps.instruction: On Windows, use the official Windows ZIP and select raze.exe with the extracted player folder as its working directory. Keep the DLLs, raze.pk3 and soundfonts together. Registration does not start the player; Play does. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your BLOOD.RFF archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

steps.title: Preserve the actual shared profile
steps.instruction: Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

steps.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
steps.instruction: You and upstream replace this external player. Portcove registration preserves every external file and does not promise managed Update, Backup or Rollback. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. Linux has no native archive in this selected GitHub release: use an already prepared upstream/system-package copy or upstream’s build instructions, then its native player. Linux normally uses ~/.config/raze for configuration and savegames, and can move an older ~/.raze directory on first use. Platform handoffs do not establish native execution or save compatibility.

A matching Dolphin-extracted Disc/DATA folder is another upstream route. Keep the original image recoverable; no original disc or automatic helper execution is supplied by Portcove. Reuse a valid remembered disc choice.

steps.title: Keep saves, SD content and mods together
steps.instruction: Close both game and launcher before copying data or replacing the runtime. Back up the complete engine/UserData tree in packaged releases, including Config.toml, NAND saves, SD and mods, plus any sd.raw card and configured custom disc, NAND or card roots. Development builds can instead use Play/UserData; use the folder opened by your actual launcher. Keep Disc and your original image separately. SD/card writes are copied back when the game exits, so wait for a clean exit. Use the upstream launcher for save import, controls and mod selection.

steps.title: Update with a recoverable working copy
steps.instruction: You or upstream own runtime updates and backups. Keep the current working copy and full data backup, prepare a new permitted version separately and verify your own progress before removing the old copy. Do not replace your data with a clean package. Portcove registration does not manage Update, Backup or Rollback; removing it leaves every external file untouched.

steps.title: Use the upstream setup for your own Dungeon Keeper
steps.instruction: The upstream Windows web installer is the simplest setup route. Follow the linked instructions, choose a separate KeeperFX folder and supply your own supported Dungeon Keeper CD, GOG, EA or Steam files. If you downloaded the complete .7z package here, extract it with your archive tool and open keeperfx-launcher.exe yourself; it prompts for the original files. steps.title: Choose the upstream launcher
steps.instruction: On Windows 10 or newer, choose keeperfx-launcher.exe from the prepared KeeperFX folder, with that folder as its working directory. It provides setup, settings and upstream updates. Save launch details in Portcove, then choose Play separately. Upstream also documents keeperfx-launcher-legacy.exe or the direct keeperfx.exe route for older environments; those are deliberate alternatives, not another required setup question.

steps.title: Preserve the external copy when updating
steps.instruction: Let the upstream launcher provide updates, and keep a separate copy of your working folder before replacing files. Preserve save (including settings.toml), keeperfx.cfg, original data, screenshots and any custom maps, campaigns or mods. Select the CD’s keeper folder when upstream asks for original CD data; other editions have their own folder rules in the linked guide. Portcove does not own these files or provide managed Update, Backup or Rollback for them.

listings.summary: Prepare a separate Cave Story player with your own supported data and preserve the chosen edition’s saves.

steps.title: Prepare a separate Cave Story folder
steps.instruction: Keep your current game and store installation. For the original freeware edition, put the downloaded doukutsu-rs Windows executable beside a copy of your Doukutsu.exe and data folder; first launch extracts the additional original resources. For supported Cave Story+ editions, use your own data folder as described by upstream. The 2026 Steam remaster is not established by this guide, and remastered saves are incompatible with original-version saves. steps.title: Add the prepared player

Keep its matching data folder in place. Linux publishes a standalone x86_64 ELF, and the Mac downloads contain separate Intel or Apple Silicon app bundles; follow the linked platform instructions for those instead of treating the Windows download as an installer.

steps.title: Keep the chosen edition and user data
steps.instruction: You own updates to this external copy. Prepare another version separately and keep your current player, original data and saves until it works. The engine normally uses the operating system’s doukutsu-rs user-data folder, or a sibling user folder in portable mode. Its Advanced menu can open the user-data folder; keep a separate backup of it, including settings.json and saves, before changing versions or editions. Portcove does not back up, roll back or delete this external game/data tree.

listings.name: Driver 2 / REDRIVER2
listings.summary: Play Driver 2 with the native REDRIVER2 player and both of your original discs.

steps.title: Keep the standard player and its dependencies together
steps.instruction: Use the standard release archive, keeping REDRIVER2.exe on Windows or REDRIVER2 on Linux with its complete data, configuration and install/ companions. The Windows player is Win32 and can run on a Windows x64 host; the Linux package is x64 and needs the upstream SDL2/OpenAL dependencies. Follow upstream instructions for any missing Windows Visual C++ runtime. Development archives are separate alternatives.

steps.title: Prepare both of your original discs with upstream setup
steps.instruction: You need both of your Driver 2 discs. Upstream documents English US/EU revisions 1.0 and 1.1. On Windows, put the upstream Launcher.exe in the player folder, install the required Java runtime for media conversion, and use its Setup wizard with both disc images. The Launcher is a separate native program; Java runs the bundled jPSXdec conversion tools. Back up a working prepared folder before allowing setup to replace its contents. Portcove never starts the Launcher, scripts or JARs during discovery.

steps.title: Use the manual setup alternative only when needed
steps.instruction: If you are not using the Windows Setup wizard, the supplied conversion scripts expect raw disc data at install/Driver2CD1.bin and install/Driver2CD2.bin, with config.ini pointing to the first image. Renaming a CHD or a cooked ISO does not convert it into the required raw data. Follow the upstream guide and deliberately run the Windows/Linux conversion step with Java to prepare the media. Review any conversion errors and keep originals and failed work recoverable before retrying.

steps.title: Add the prepared player, then choose Play
steps.instruction: Register REDRIVER2.exe or the Linux REDRIVER2 executable with its complete prepared folder as the working directory. Keep the upstream Launcher for its setup and configuration functions. Read-only discovery only suggests a launch target; saving launch details and choosing Play remain separate choices.

steps.title: Preserve your prepared copy and actual profile
steps.instruction: You or upstream provide runtime updates. Keep the whole prepared folder, config.ini, cutscene_recorder.ini, original images, generated media, mods and any custom data-folder paths before trying a new version separately. Profiles live under USERPROFILE/.driver2 on Windows or HOME/.driver2 on Linux, including config.dat and progress.dat; they are not isolated by choosing another player folder. Preserve that actual profile too. Portcove registration provides no managed Update, Backup or Rollback, and removing it leaves every external file untouched.

listings.name: Duke Nukem 3D (Raze)
listings.summary: Play Duke Nukem 3D in Raze using your own original PC game files.

steps.title: Use your recognized original game files
steps.instruction: Use your own original PC Duke Nukem 3D data folder, anchored by DUKE3D.GRP. Raze recognizes retail 1.3/Atomic and specific World Tour data variants; the actual group-file identity selects the edition. Keep the accompanying original files. Console, mobile and other Raze games are not substitutes. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze, or add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

steps.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
steps.instruction: On Windows, use the official Windows ZIP and select raze.exe with the extracted player folder as its working directory. Keep the DLLs, raze.pk3 and soundfonts together. Registration does not start the player; Play does. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your DUKE3D.GRP archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

steps.title: Preserve the actual shared profile
steps.instruction: Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

steps.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
steps.instruction: You and upstream replace this external player. Portcove registration preserves every external file and does not promise managed Update, Backup or Rollback. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. Linux has no native archive in this selected GitHub release: use an already prepared upstream/system-package copy or upstream’s build instructions, then its native player. Linux normally uses ~/.config/raze for configuration and savegames, and can move an older ~/.raze directory on first use. Platform handoffs do not establish native execution or save compatibility.

steps.title: Use a permitted copy and your matching game files
steps.instruction: Keep an existing permitted complete native player, including its resources and libraries. The Windows player is MikuPan.exe; register it with its folder as the working directory. Save launch details, then choose Play separately. Prepare your own IMG_HD.BIN and IMG_BD.BIN from the matching Fatal Frame disc in a separate retained data folder. steps.title: Choose the original-data folder on first Play
steps.instruction: The native player asks for the folder containing the missing game files on first deliberate Play and remembers your selection. Keep that original-data folder outside any separately managed runtime so replacing a player does not replace your originals. The package is portable and has no installer. Source builds have their own CMake/dependency instructions. Linux is a separate upstream route; macOS is an experimental Apple Silicon community build with no maintained hardware coverage, not Windows qualification.

steps.title: Back up the actual profile before updating
steps.instruction: You or upstream update this external copy. Close the game, keep the working folder, and extract a new permitted player separately. Back up the SDL profile for Mikompilation/MikuPan, including mikupan.ini, memory-card saves, albums and PNG captures; on Windows this is normally under AppData/Roaming. If SDL cannot supply a profile directory, upstream uses the local MikuPan directory instead; retain that too. Preserve the original-data folder separately. External registration leaves every file untouched and provides no managed Update, Backup or Rollback. Runtime replacement does not rewind saves or establish older-version readability.

steps.title: Keep the game profile when updating
steps.instruction: You or upstream update this external copy. An existing portable copy can use its own folder instead; retain the mode you already use. Keep the ROM, settings, saves and mods together with that profile. The game can import a compatible save through Settings → Saves before starting; its existing save is retained as hybridheaven.us.bin.pre-import.bak. Controller Pak .mpk files are not accepted by that importer. Verify progress in the new copy before retiring the old one. steps.title: Import your own game on first Play
steps.instruction: The official Windows x64 ZIP is portable and has no installer. Choose InfiniteUndiscoveryRecomp.exe and keep its DLLs and notices together. On first Play, the game’s integrated wizard validates and imports your own Disc 1 from a supported XDVDFS ISO or extracted folder; Disc 2 and A/B Voucher DLC are optional. It identifies supported USA, USA-UNDUB, Europe, Japan and Asia editions from the media. Do not mix editions. Portcove does not run an extraction helper or developer compiler. Windows 10/11 x64 and Direct3D 12 are required; use Microsoft’s Visual C++ 2015–2022 x64 Redistributable if the documented runtime DLLs are missing.

steps.title: Keep each content profile together
steps.instruction: The complete portable folder holds setup.json and separate USA, USA-UNDUB, EUROPE, JAPAN and ASIA profiles. Each configured profile owns its imported assets/DLC, saves and configuration. Keep cache/runtime.toml too: it contains runtime settings despite the cache folder name. Close the game before updates or copying data. Keep interrupted import/staging folders recoverable and consult upstream; do not merge different editions. Backups can include large original-game files and DLC, so keep them private. The separate IU Save Bridge companion is optional and is not run by Portcove.

steps.title: Update an existing copy safely
steps.instruction: For a copy you register yourself, you or upstream provide updates. Extract a new official player into a separate folder, keep the working copy, and follow the selected release’s instructions for carrying its complete compatible content profiles and setup.json. Do not copy old runtime DLLs or shader caches over the replacement. Runtime rollback does not rewind saves or guarantee that older software can read them. The selected release-tag documentation had not tested the Disc 1 to Disc 2 transition. Later upstream documentation at 614a0a0ebd72103fce8aaa52c715d847b703a53e reports repeated successful transitions, while complete Disc 2 progression and a full playthrough remain unverified and a Vesplume Tower / Orb of Patience softlock remains under investigation. These are upstream reports; Portcove has not run the game.

listings.name: NAM (Raze)
listings.summary: Play NAM in Raze using your own original PC game files.

steps.title: Use your recognized original game files
steps.instruction: Use your own original PC NAM data folder, anchored by NAM.GRP. Keep its accompanying original files. Upstream also recognizes the distinct NAPALM.GRP edition; select the actual owned edition in Raze rather than renaming or substituting another game’s data. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze, or add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

steps.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
steps.instruction: On Windows, use the official Windows ZIP and select raze.exe with the extracted player folder as its working directory. Keep the DLLs, raze.pk3 and soundfonts together. Registration does not start the player; Play does. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your NAM.GRP archive (NAPALM.GRP for that owned edition). Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

steps.title: Preserve the actual shared profile
steps.instruction: Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

steps.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
steps.instruction: You and upstream replace this external player. Portcove registration preserves every external file and does not promise managed Update, Backup or Rollback. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. Linux has no native archive in this selected GitHub release: use an already prepared upstream/system-package copy or upstream’s build instructions, then its native player. Linux normally uses ~/.config/raze for configuration and savegames, and can move an older ~/.raze directory on first use. Platform handoffs do not establish native execution or save compatibility.

steps.title: Use the fork's own launcher and game-file setup
steps.instruction: Use the official package for your platform from the shared macos-nightly release; that historical tag also contains Windows and Linux packages. On Windows, extract the complete ZIP and deliberately open ApeEscapeRecomp.exe to reach its launcher. On Linux, follow the AppImage instructions, enable execution when your desktop requires it and open the AppImage itself. Select your own North American Ape Escape disc, SCUS-94423; keep a CUE and its matching BIN together and choose the CUE. A cooked 2048-byte ISO discards needed sectors. steps.title: Keep the macOS application handoff intact
steps.instruction: On macOS, use the official DMG, drag Ape Escape Recompiled.app into Applications and deliberately open it through macOS, including its normal opening confirmation for this ad-hoc-signed preview. The app's shell entry seeds the player-data folder and sets required environment values before starting its native player. Use that supported app entry. Do not register the private Contents/MacOS/ApeEscapeRecomp.bin as a substitute or bypass the wrapper. Portcove's existing native-file registration does not supply this shell/app-bundle invocation; macOS remains an upstream application/instructions handoff.

steps.title: Register supported existing players without changing their owner
steps.instruction: For Windows, register ApeEscapeRecomp.exe with the extracted package folder as its working directory. For Linux, register the prepared AppImage itself; do not select its internal AppRun or another extracted helper. Registration is separate from Play and preserves the external files. This enhanced maintained fork is distinct from mstan's original integration; it does not replace or migrate an existing parent installation.

steps.title: Use upstream updates and back up the actual data folder
steps.instruction: Use the fork's Nightly update interface on supported Windows/macOS builds; older builds may need a new upstream package first. Linux AppImage replacement remains manual. Keep generated overlay caches, configuration and mods with their upstream-supported workflow; they are not a generic managed runtime/data replacement contract. Windows game saves/configuration remain beside the player; Linux game data uses $XDG_DATA_HOME/ApeEscapeRecomp or ~/.local/share/ApeEscapeRecomp unless APE_ESCAPE_RECOMP_DATA_DIR overrides it. On Windows and Linux, launcher preferences and updater rollback metadata also use a separate per-user NVDEMU/Ape Escape Recompiled - Enhanced Edition folder under the platform app-data root, or the same explicit override. Preserve both actual roots. The separate launcher-data defaults are %APPDATA%/NVDEMU/Ape Escape Recompiled - Enhanced Edition on Windows, and $XDG_DATA_HOME/NVDEMU/Ape Escape Recompiled - Enhanced Edition or ~/.local/share/NVDEMU/Ape Escape Recompiled - Enhanced Edition on Linux; preserve the explicit override instead when set. macOS uses ~/Library/Application Support/Ape Escape Recompiled through its app wrapper. listings.summary: Play PowerSlave / Exhumed (DOS) in Raze using your own original PC game files.

steps.title: Use your recognized original game files
steps.instruction: Use your own DOS PowerSlave or Exhumed data folder, anchored by STUFF.DAT. Raze recognizes the distinct supported PowerSlave and Exhumed data identities. Keep the complete accompanying original data. The Saturn/PlayStation games and the 2022 Exhumed remaster are different implementations/data contracts. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze, or add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

steps.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
steps.instruction: On Windows, use the official Windows ZIP and select raze.exe with the extracted player folder as its working directory. Keep the DLLs, raze.pk3 and soundfonts together. Registration does not start the player; Play does. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your STUFF.DAT archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

steps.title: Preserve the actual shared profile
steps.instruction: Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

steps.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
steps.instruction: You and upstream replace this external player. Portcove registration preserves every external file and does not promise managed Update, Backup or Rollback. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. Linux has no native archive in this selected GitHub release: use an already prepared upstream/system-package copy or upstream’s build instructions, then its native player. Linux normally uses ~/.config/raze for configuration and savegames, and can move an older ~/.raze directory on first use. Platform handoffs do not establish native execution or save compatibility.

Follow the upstream Linux profile and update instructions and preserve the current copy. Portcove’s managed Windows route does not manage this wrapper.

listings.name: Shadow Warrior (Raze)
listings.summary: Play Shadow Warrior in Raze using your own original PC game files.

steps.title: Use your recognized original game files
steps.instruction: Use your own 1997 PC Shadow Warrior data folder, anchored by SW.GRP. Keep its accompanying files and any separately owned expansion data. The 2013 reboot is a different game. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze, or add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

steps.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
steps.instruction: On Windows, use the official Windows ZIP and select raze.exe with the extracted player folder as its working directory. Keep the DLLs, raze.pk3 and soundfonts together. Registration does not start the player; Play does. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your SW.GRP archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

steps.title: Preserve the actual shared profile
steps.instruction: Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

steps.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
steps.instruction: You and upstream replace this external player. Portcove registration preserves every external file and does not promise managed Update, Backup or Rollback. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. Linux has no native archive in this selected GitHub release: use an already prepared upstream/system-package copy or upstream’s build instructions, then its native player. Linux normally uses ~/.config/raze for configuration and savegames, and can move an older ~/.raze directory on first use. Platform handoffs do not establish native execution or save compatibility.

listings.summary: Explore Glover / Glover-R (ThatGuyMcd) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Select your own Glover ROM on first Play
steps.instruction: Choose Play, then select your own unmodified Glover USA revision 0 ROM when the game asks. The launcher accepts .z64, .n64 and .v64 byte order for this 8 MiB NGVE cartridge (canonical SHA-1 270be17b3c8da9b88a7b99c2a545b0bce16837f4). The published Windows player needs no game build or separate installer. Configure controls in the launcher or press F1/Escape while playing; use its Mods page for compatible mods and separate mod profiles.

steps.title: Keep your saves and mod profiles safe
steps.instruction: Default Windows saves, settings, mod profiles, mod-specific saves, logs and crash reports use %APPDATA%/Glover-R. Keep a separate backup of that profile before changing versions; an older runtime may not read newer data. Optional custom configuration and developer paths need their own backup. Keep customized existing copies registered with their own launch details.

steps.title: Linux uses the upstream AppImage route
steps.instruction: Use the Linux x86-64 AppImage, or extract the Linux Portable archive and deliberately run Launch-Glover-R.sh. That archive contains an AppImage and wrapper, rather than a bare player with ordinary libraries. The wrapper uses AppImage extraction mode when a normal AppImage launch is unavailable. Steam Deck uses its separate x86-64 package and START-GLOVER-R.sh. Linux saves/settings normally use $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/glover-r or ~/.config/glover-r; preserve that actual profile separately. Follow upstream updates for this copy; the Windows managed route does not manage the Linux wrapper or infer device/gameplay support.

listings.name: Doom / UZDoom (UZDoom)
listings.summary: Choose your own Doom-family game data and mods in UZDoom; the upstream launcher provides runtime updates.

steps.title: Use the upstream-owned player
steps.instruction: Extract the complete official Windows x64 archive into a separate folder. Choose uzdoom.exe with that folder as its working directory and save launch details, then choose Play deliberately. updater.exe is the upstream runtime replacement helper, not the player to register. Other upstream platforms use their own AppImage or Mac disk-image setup; this Windows package does not establish their operation.

steps.title: Choose your game data
steps.instruction: Use the launcher to select your own supported IWAD or compatible free game data. Keep mods and game data under the upstream documented setup. Adding launch details does not start a game; choose Play separately.

steps.title: Update through upstream
steps.instruction: UZDoom’s launcher checks for updates and can use updater.exe to replace package files. Keep that runtime ownership with upstream. Portcove leaves these external files untouched and offers no managed Update, Backup or Rollback promise for them. Before changing versions, close the game and back up your actual IWADs, mods and configured save paths. Windows normally stores uzdoom.ini under Documents/My Games/UZDoom and saves under the Windows Saved Games/UZDoom folder. Portable mode uses uzdoom_portable.ini and the local Save and Screenshots folders. Custom config/save overrides and relocated Windows user folders need their own backup. Keep the working copy recoverable; upstream update_backup is not a Portcove-verified player-data backup.

Keep settings and saves together and retain a working copy before replacing it. Portcove does not adopt or back up these files, rewind saves or guarantee older-runtime readability.

listings.name: World War II GI (Raze)
listings.summary: Play World War II GI in Raze using your own original PC game files.

steps.title: Use your recognized original game files
steps.instruction: Use your own original PC WWII GI data folder, anchored by WW2GI.GRP. Keep its accompanying files. Platoon Leader is an optional separately owned expansion that depends on the base game; it is not required for this base-game entry. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze, or add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

steps.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
steps.instruction: On Windows, use the official Windows ZIP and select raze.exe with the extracted player folder as its working directory. Keep the DLLs, raze.pk3 and soundfonts together. Registration does not start the player; Play does. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your WW2GI.GRP archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

steps.title: Preserve the actual shared profile
steps.instruction: Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

steps.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
steps.instruction: You and upstream replace this external player. Portcove registration preserves every external file and does not promise managed Update, Backup or Rollback. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. Linux has no native archive in this selected GitHub release: use an already prepared upstream/system-package copy or upstream’s build instructions, then its native player. Linux normally uses ~/.config/raze for configuration and savegames, and can move an older ~/.raze directory on first use. Platform handoffs do not establish native execution or save compatibility.

listings.name: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past / Zelda 3 Reborn / Z3R (xander-haj)
listings.summary: Prepare Zelda 3 Reborn with your own USA A Link to the Past ROM and the upstream launcher.

steps.title: Let the upstream launcher prepare your own game
steps.instruction: The recommended Windows download is the upstream lawn/Z3R Launcher setup package. Open that installer deliberately after downloading, then use its guided preparation. Install its published package for your platform, choose your own clean USA A Link to the Past .sfc, and follow its setup/extract/build steps. The Windows setup package includes the lightweight Git/Python/TCC/SDL2 toolkit; choosing a separate MSBuild route needs its own build tools. Linux and macOS use their matching upstream dependency guide. Portcove does not install these tools or run the launcher during discovery. When setup finishes, register the prepared zelda3.exe on Windows or native zelda3 player on Linux/macOS with its project folder as the working directory, then choose Play explicitly.

steps.title: Keep the generated assets and player data together
steps.instruction: Keep the complete prepared project, your original ROM, zelda3_assets.dat, zelda3.user.ini overrides, saves, custom sprites/shaders/MSU packs, and any randomizer YAML, seed/spoiler files or selected feature-asset folders separately backed up. The game tries zelda3.user.ini before zelda3.ini. Keep packaged defaults with their own release and use user overrides for personal settings. The native release ZIP supplies a player and SDL but no generated zelda3_assets.dat; copying that executable alone is not finished setup.

steps.title: Regenerate matching assets when updating
steps.instruction: Let the selected upstream launcher manage its own project setup and updates. The game’s guide requires asset regeneration after relevant executable/source, extraction-script, YAML or INI behavior changes. Copying an older generated asset file into a replacement runtime cannot satisfy that requirement. Preserve the old prepared copy and randomizer choices before regeneration; extracting clean ROM data after randomizing overwrites the randomized YAML. Portcove registers the prepared player without claiming Update, Backup or Rollback for these externally owned files. The related Python Z3R-Launcher and current lawn delivery are helpers for this same engine identity, not extra games. The launcher’s Updates action uses its matching platform installer or self-replacement route; keep that owner. Its download feed follows releases without a fixed tag in this listing.
